allowedSourceMaterial.overview: Varda focuses her eye on gleaners: those who scour already-reaped fields for the odd potato or turnip. Her investigation leads from forgotten corners of the French countryside to off-hours at the green markets of Paris, following those who insist on finding a use for that which society has cast off, whether out of necessity or activism.

semanticBoundaryFlags.message: Observational documentary pacing could also support easy-watch; alone was chosen on the strength of the personal eye-led journey, but a human reviewer should confirm.

visibleEditorialCopy.curiosityHook: What drives modern gleaners across fields and urban stalls to recover what society routinely abandons?
visibleEditorialCopy.description: Director Agnès Varda travels from rural French fields to Parisian green markets, documenting gleaners who salvage discarded produce and forgotten objects out of necessity or activism.
visibleEditorialCopy.vibeSummary: Thoughtful, deliberate, and grounded; an engaged French documentary that rewards patient solo viewing.
visibleEditorialCopy.whyWatch: Varda turns an intimate, wandering documentary inquiry into an observant meditation on waste, resourcefulness, and the varied lives making purpose out of what others leave behind.
